verdict.rationale: Flagsmith's experimentation docs say A/B test results are read through a built-in Bayesian statistics engine, fed by events collected into a managed data warehouse. That covers the core of having a stats engine behind experiment results. However, the pack only names the engine and never documents its methodology. Missing for 10: any variance-reduction options (e.g. CUPED), documented statistical methodology detail (priors, decision thresholds, metric handling), any frequentist option, and independent or hands-on corroboration of result trustworthiness.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can trust a documented statistics engine (Bayesian or frequentist, with variance-reduction options) behind experiment results

citations.quote: Flagsmith Experimentation lets you run A/B tests end to end on the platform: serve variations of a feature with a multivariate flag, collect events from your application into a managed data warehouse, and read the results with a built-in Bayesian statistics engine.
read the results with a built-in Bayesian statistics engine
